name: Cavalier Lord-Protector
body:
Cavaliers are noble warriors that travel the land taking on incredible challenges and surmounting them. The lord-protector challenge those that would bring harm to their allies and stops them with their force of arms.

Mettle (Ex)

At 1st level, a lord-protector gains a Mettle pool that is refreshed each day. The pool’s maximum is equal to their Charisma modifier, plus any feats and special abilities that increases the pool maximum. Some abilities may restore points to this pool during the day. But the lord protector may not have more points of Mettle than the pool’s maximum.

The lord-protector may expend Mettle to gain one of the following benefits.

As an immediate action they may gain a bonus equal to their Charisma modifier on the next saving throw. The bonus must be used before the beginning of their next turn.
As part of making a Strength or Dexterity check to gain a bonus equal to their Charisma bonus on that check. The lord-protector may restore a point of Mettle to your pool in the following ways.
If they use the aid another action to assist an ally’s skill check and the ally would have failed the check without their action
If the lord-protector uses the aid another action to improve an ally’s AC and the ally would have been hit without the their action
If the target of their challenge is a creature with a CR equal to the their Character Level +2 and they are victorious in the encounter without falling unconscious.

If an ability which expends Mettle allows for the use of an attack of opportunity, the attack of opportunity allowed by that ability may be taken even while using the total defense action.

Protector’s Challenge (Ex)

At 1st level, a lordprotector uses a point of Mettle to enact their cavalier’s challenge instead of having a per-day use. This ability modifies the challenge ability of the cavalier, but any other archetype that replaces the ability may still be taken but instead uses Mettle.

Valorous Deflection (Ex)

At 1st level, when an opponent makes a melee attack against the lordprotector or an adjacent ally, they can spend a point of Mettle and a use of an attack of opportunity to attempt to parry the attack. They make an attack roll as if they were making an attack of opportunity. For each size category the attacking creature is larger, the lordprotector takes a -2 penalty to this attack. If the attempt is made using a shield attack, the lordprotector may apply any enhancement or ability bonuses to shield AC to the attack. If the attack result is greater than the attackers, the attack automatically misses. The attempt must be declared before the results of the attack are known.

If this attack is made while they are using the Combat Expertise feat, fighting defensively, or taking the total defense action they may also add the bonus from those abilities to the attack roll to block an attack, but loses any used bonuses until the beginning of their next turn.

Upon a successful parry, if the lord-protector has at least one point of Mettle they may make a riposte attack on the creature they parried as an immediate action, provided the target is in their threatened area. If the parry attempt fails, the attack is instead directed at the lord-protector at its normal result and the guardian is flat-footed and loses their shield bonus to AC if the shield was used in the attempt.

This ability replaces the tactician ability for the cavalier.

The following two abilities replace the mount ability for the cavalier.

Shield Focus (Ex)

The lord-protector is a master of defense. At 1st level, they gain Shield Focus as a bonus feat. At 8th level and every 6 levels thereafter the bonus granted by the Shield Focus feat increases by an additional +1. They only receive this additional benefit on one wielded shield.

Weapons of the Guardian (Ex)

At 2nd level, the lord-protector gains Improved Shield Bash and Two-Weapon Fighting as bonus feats. Additionally, they may treat heavy shields as light weapons for the purposes of two-weapon fighting penalties as long as they wield only one shield. At 7th level, the lord-protector gains Improved Two-Weapon Fighting and at 12th level, they gain Greater Two-Weapon Fighting as bonus feats.

They do not need to meet the prerequisites for these bonus feats, though these feats only apply when wielding a shield in one hand.

The following ability replaces the mount ability.

Furious Focus (Ex)

At 1st level, the lord-protector gains Power Attack and Furious Focus as a bonus feats.

At 6th level and every four thereafter the lord-protector reduces the penalty on all attack rolls from the Power Attack feat by 1 (minimum -0).

Behind Me (Ex)

At 2nd level, the lord-protector may elect to place themselves in the path of danger in order to protect an ally. When rolling initiative, the lord-protector may select a target as a charge. This selection may not change for the duration of the encounter. Any time that they are within 5 feet of their charge, and the charge is the target of an attack, the lord-protector may, as an immediate action, enter the square occupied by the charge and receive the attack in their place. The attack automatically hits the lordprotector. The charge is placed in any empty square adjacent to the lord-protector of their choice. They may activate this ability after knowing whether their charge will be hit.

If the lord-protector suffers a critical hit as a result of using behind me they restore a point of Mettle.

This ability replaces the bravery granted at 2nd level.

Trial by Combat (Ex)

At 4th level, the lord-protector can shout a challenge to all enemies within 100 feet that can both see and hear them as a standard action. This appeals to the enemy’s pride, narcissism, fear, anger or other emotions and paints the lord-protector as a threat to be vanquished. This only affects enemies who would be subject to the lord-protector’s protector’s challenge ability and expends a point of Mettle to activate. Each enemy to be affected must make a Will save equal to 10 + 1/2 the lord-protector’s class level + their Charisma modifier. Each enemy that fails must attack the lordprotector or include them in the area of effect of a spell or special ability that doesn’t target creatures.

An enemy under the effects of trial by combat can choose not to attack lord-protector and instead spend a standard action calming their emotions and rolling a new save. Otherwise, trial by combat lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 the lord-protector’s class levels + their Charisma modifier.

If the lord-protector is rendered unconscious by damage taken from targets under the effect of trial by combat, they restore two points of Mettle.

This ability replaces the expert trainer ability of the cavalier or the mounted archer ability of the samurai.

Active Defense (Ex)

At 6th level, a lord-protector may spend a point of Mettle as an immediate action to apply any shield bonus they benefit from to their CMD and touch AC for a number of rounds equal to their Charisma modifier. They may activate this ability even while grappled or otherwise restrained so long as they are still benefiting from a shield bonus.

Starting at 11th level, the lord-protector may apply this bonus to themselves and one adjacent ally.

Additionally, this ability now adds their shield bonus to Reflex saves during duration.

Starting at 16th level, the lord-protector’s shield bonus always applies to their own CMD, touch AC and Reflex saving throws. They may now expend a use of Mettle to apply this bonus to up to two adjacent allies.

If the lord-protector has levels in another class that provides this ability, their effective class levels stack.

This ability replaces the combat feat gained at 6th level for both the cavalier and the samurai.

Brace (Ex)

At 9th level, if the lord-protector succeeds on a Reflex save against a spell or effect while wielding a shield they may expend a point of Mettle as an immediate action to prevent that effect from affecting all squares adjacent to them as well as negating the effect fully on themselves.

This ability replaces the greater tactician ability for the cavalier, not the samurai.

Follow Through (Ex)

At 9th level, whenever the lord-protector deals damage with a two handed melee weapon they add twice their strength bonus to the damage roll rather than one and a half times.

This ability replaces greater resolve for the samurai, but not the cavalier.

Death Before Dishonor (Ex)

At 11th level, the lordprotector gains Diehard as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. At any time while the Diehard feat is active, the lord-protector may expend a point of Mettle to suppress the staggered condition for the round. Any strenuous action still causes damage as normal.

Additionally, if the lord-protector’s hit points are below their Constitution score, they may expend a point of Mettle each round to continue to act under the Diehard feat until they reach a negative hp total equal to their lord-protector class levels plus their Constitution score. During this time, they may still expend additional Mettle to suppress the staggered condition.

If the lord-protector does not expend Mettle while still within this threshold, they are considered dying and stable for one round. If they do not receive healing within the round to bring their hit points back above their Constitution score, they die.

This ability replaces the mighty charge ability of the cavalier or the honorable stand ability of the samurai.

Bring ‘em Down (Ex)

At 12th level, the lordprotector is able to defend their immediate area against all who would attempt to force their way by. As long as the lord-protector has a point of mettle they may make attacks of opportunity against foes that enter their threatened area even if under the effect of a spell or ability that otherwise prevents attacks of opportunity such as Fly-by Attack or Improved Grapple. If this attack hits, the lord-protector may expend a point of Mettle to deal damage as normal and if the attack roll would also beat the target’s CMD, they are tripped.

This ability allows the lord-protector to trip flying creatures. A flying creature tripped by this ability falls to the ground.

This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 12th level for both the cavalier and the samurai.

Overwhelming Presence (Ex)

At 17th level, as a swift action the lord-protector may spend 2 points of Mettle to project their superior skill and strength of arms to all enemies, weeding out the weak and allowing only the strong to face them. All enemies within 60 feet of the lord-protector must make a Will save (DC equal to 10 + 1/2 their class levels + their Charisma modifier) or become shaken until the end of combat. Any creature that fails its save by 5 or more or has fewer HD than the lord-protector’s character level minus 4 is frightened for 1 minute. Afterwards they become shaken as long as they can see and hear the lordprotector. Regardless of the outcome, this ability can only affect a given creature once every 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect, though it can affect any creature with an Intelligence score regardless of immunity, in such a case the creature can only become shaken.

This ability replaces the master tactician ability of the cavalier or the true resolve ability of the samurai.

Lord-Protector of the Realm (Ex)

At 20th level, a lord-protector of the realm is known far and wide. The lord-protector gains an alignment aura as a cleric of the same level. Any weapon they wield is treated as aligned (using one of their alignment descriptors of the lordprotector if any), people who share an alignment descriptor with the lord-protector always have a starting attitude of at least indifferent to the lordprotector unless they have been given direct orders to oppose the lord-protector and their allies, and lastly, they no longer need to expend Mettle to activate challenge, behind me, and trial by combat.

This ability replaces the supreme charge ability of the cavalier or the last stand ability of the samurai.
